title: In-place array update
summary: Proves the compiler's in-place templates for set!, eraseIdxIfInBounds, insertIdx!, and push on an owned array at its last use: one store; a loop that moves the later elements down and a shorter length; for insertIdx! and push, a move to a block of twice the capacity when full, then for insertIdx! a loop that moves the later elements up from the top down, and the new element and a longer length.
premises: heap.Owned for the array the call hands over, and Heap.At
A memory cap of at most 65,535 pages, and alloc and release at functions 0 and 1, for insertIdx! and push
Locals for the length, the loop, and the growth path below scratch and apart from the array, position, and value
result: Stmt.AppendPost for the updated array: owned at the same pointer, or for an insert or push into a full block at a new one, with every region apart from the old block kept and apart from the result.
